text.p: Ford Motor Co. said Wednesday it is recalling 27,553 Expedition full-size sport utility vehicles in the United States and Canada because some attachments in the frame and axle parts were not welded properly.

If the welds in both problem areas were to break, the rear frame and body could move sideways and affect vehicle control, Ford said. If one of the welds separated, the car might sway during lane changes.
About 1,639 of the recalled vehicles are in Canada. It is the first recall of the popular sport utility vehicle since it officially went on sale in September 1996.

Since production began, Ford has made 110,000 of the vehicles. The vehicles included in the recall were made between March 1 and Oct. 10 of 1996. Expeditions are made at Ford's Michigan Truck plant in Wayne, Mich.
Ford spokeswoman Karen Shaughnessy said no accidents or injuries have been reported as result of the problems.
Ford's stock egded down 12.5 cents to $33.375 on the New York Stock Exchange.
